claims.text: Local compositional inhomogeneity governs the onset of premelting and complete melting in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Short-range elemental clustering lowers the energy barrier for formation of partial-melting sites.
Short-range chemical clustering can occur in multicomponent high-entropy alloys over a wide temperature range.
Heat treatment can alter short-range chemical order in concentrated multicomponent alloys.
Controlled heat treatments can produce HEA nanoparticles having different degrees of local clustering while retaining identical size distributions.
Short-range chemical clustering produces local lattice distortion.
Clustering-associated lattice distortion creates sites of incipient melting.
Elemental-distribution inhomogeneities locally reduce the free energy for phase change.
The locally reduced phase-change free energy permits molten regions to appear at lower temperatures.
Initially formed molten regions subsequently expand and drive complete melting.
Clustered HEA nanoparticles will show more noticeable premelting features than homogenized nanoparticles.
Clustered HEA nanoparticles will begin melting tens of degrees earlier than homogenized nanoparticles.
The degree of local clustering will correlate with both the extent and temperature of premelting.
Homogenized HEA nanoparticles will exhibit a higher and sharper melting temperature than clustered particles.
Homogenized HEA nanoparticles will exhibit reduced premelting features.
The proposed clustering-controlled behavior should hold for approximately 10–50 nm nanoparticles containing at least five metals with varying mixing enthalpies.
In substantially larger particles or alloys with fewer elements, surface-related melting or phase-separation effects may prevail over clustering-controlled melting.
Particle shape, surface oxidation, and support interactions may mask or modify the effect of clustering on melting.
Equivalent melting onsets and absence of a clustering–premelting correlation would falsify the proposed governing role of compositional inhomogeneity.
